answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks using memory-hard proof-of-work challenges. Even across distributed deployments monitoring willow groves or vine crops, agents must compute memory-bound graph cycles to register. An attacker incurs the scarce cost of provisioning dedicated RAM and power per alias, while peers track the verification delta to discard delayed responses. However, this approach burdens low-power edge nodes and cannot stop adversaries with massive hardware budgets.
